text:
maya: Heads-up, a weird stop/EOS failure cropped up during quantized bring-up for hf/model-x-q4. Streaming responses cut off early on a small set of prompts.

alex: Seen this. Is it the tokenizer emitting multiple eos tokens or runtime misdetecting partial stop strings?

maya: Repro steps I ran locally: converted HF -> Redwood format, used our streaming endpoint. For some prompts we get a single short token then stream ends. Tokenizer show: `tokenizer.encode('\n') -> [301, 301]` (two identical special tokens).

ryan: two identical tokens is suspicious. Which special token are we mapping to EOS in config.json?

maya: In the HF config.json it had \"eos_token\": \"\", \"eos_token_id\": 302. But tokenizer's internal split for some unicode sequences gave 301/302 mixes depending on chunk boundary.

sam: Also saw an issue where our streaming chunker splits multi-byte bytes so stop matches inside chunk boundary trigger `stop_on_eos` even when remainder of the token arrives next chunk. That causes premature termination.

alex: Can you paste the minimal repro call you used?

maya: Sure — local snippet (pseudo):
```
resp = redwood.stream_generate(model='model-x-q4', input='Hello 👋\n\n', stream_handler=handler)
# handler receives: 'Hello ', '\n' then stream closed early
```

maya: On inspection the tokenizer produced an extra eos-like token when emoji+newline combo was present. Quantized kernels seem to fold repeated eos byte patterns into a single output token in some code paths.

ryan: That explains it. Quantization fused-kernel heuristics can change emission timing for sentinel tokens. We should decouple streaming stop detection from raw token equality and instead reconstruct text chunks before checking stop sequences.

sam: Agreed. Short-term patch: in runtime, buffer the last N bytes of the previous chunk and check the reconstructed text for stop sequences instead of relying on token ids. Also add a flag to disable `stop_on_eos` for models where eos_token_id maps to multiple token ids.

alex: For onboarding checklist, add: verify `special_tokens_map` in tokenizer config, ensure `eos_token` canonical string is present, and run the streaming overlap test (emoji/newline combos).

maya: I added a unit test that simulates chunk boundaries and multi-token eos: it checks that the streamer only stops when the full eos string is observed in reconstructed text. CI caught one regression.

ci-bot: Test run: streaming-eos-overlap — failed on model-x-q4 (quantized).

ryan: Ok I can push a small runtime change: increase streaming chunk reassembly window to 8 bytes and fall back to string matching for stops. Pushing patch to `eng-ml/streaming-eos-fix` branch.

sam: Another mitigation: update our HF conversion tool to prefer `eos_token` textual match (when present) and include a `stop_tokens` array in converted model metadata — Accelerator will check both token-id and string matches.

alex: Thanks. Once we have a patch, let's re-run the regression suite and a 1k-prompt smoke test focusing on chat templates and multi-eos sequences (e.g., systems that append `\n\n` as a delimiter).

maya: Filing a follow-up: I've created an internal eval with 200 examples that previously failed, saved under `evals/streaming-eos-handshake/model-x-q4/`. I'll post results after Ryan's runtime patch lands. :thumbsup:

ryan: Will ping when branch is up. If anyone sees other strange early stops, drop examples here and include both token ids and reconstructed text.

alex: Nice root cause chain: tokenizer special token mapping + quantized emission timing + chunk boundary string split. Good to have a deterministic fix path.

maya: Thanks all.
